claims.text: Formation of a heterogeneous lattice structure influences the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
A heterogeneous lattice structure enhances both strength and ductility.
The proposed enhancement arises through solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion.
The initial material is an as-cast or wrought high-entropy alloy with homogeneous composition.
Thermal or mechanical processing can induce lattice distortion.
Thermal or mechanical processing can form a heterogeneous lattice structure.
Under room-temperature uniaxial tensile loading, the processed heterogeneous-lattice alloy will have greater tensile strength than a homogeneous-lattice baseline.
Under room-temperature uniaxial tensile loading, the processed heterogeneous-lattice alloy will have greater ductility than a homogeneous-lattice baseline.
The hypothesis is intended to apply to multi-principal-element high-entropy alloys processed under conditions that induce lattice distortion.
Failure of the heterogeneous-lattice alloy to improve both strength and ductility relative to the homogeneous-lattice baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
